searchText: if you scoped down a project to appropriate size you would definitely learn a lot about how all this stuff works 🙂 I've been trying to find a good explainer of bonsai tries, does it affect blocksize? or just queries? Hi there. From my personal experience my only advice is to find a blockchain open-source project that you're interested in and start contributing. And learn on the go As you said, there is so much theory out there, you'll never be able to catch up with all of it You just need to pick something and start making the world a ~~better~~newer place 😉 <@!403707149043105803> I should have a better explainer up, but i've been heads down getting it at least full loop, then other issues got in the way. It impacts disk storage size. No intermediate hashes outside the current block are stored and we use rollback logs to work with re-orgs. These rollback logs have the potential to drive witness style trace executions (without the actual, you know, witness proof) but the besu team is still finishing that part of the project before the db format is finalized. The disc impacts are >10x total size for a full sync, much less for an initial fast sync. Disc growth rates are much more sustainable than besu's old full-forest technique. cc: <@!494908382889639977> There is also a 30% or so performance increase at mainnet scale for block processing. Not the original design intent but to a degree an expected improvement as a side effect of disc storage size and table partitioning. Oh wow thats nice Thanks <@403707149043105803>!

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: I should have a better explainer up, but i've been heads down getting it at least full loop, then other issues got in the way.  It impacts disk storage size.  No intermediate hashes outside the current block are stored and we use rollback logs to work with re-orgs.  These rollback logs have the potential to drive witness style trace executions (without the actual, you know, witness proof) but the besu team is still finishing that part of the project before the db format is finalized.

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: The disc impacts are >10x total size for a full sync, much less for an initial fast sync.  Disc growth rates are much more sustainable than besu's old full-forest technique.

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: There is also a 30% or so performance increase at mainnet scale for block processing.  Not the original design intent but to a degree an expected improvement as a side effect of disc storage size and table partitioning.
